text: Given valid PayPal credential headers and a minimal {currency, amount} order payload, When paypal_create_order is called, Then it returns the order's id and a status in {CREATED, PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED}, and the response JSON contains no client secret.
Given a real PayPal sandbox app, When paypal_create_order is called end to end, Then a real order appears in the PayPal sandbox dashboard with matching id and amount.
steps: Obtain a PayPal sandbox app Client ID/Secret (needs a real vendor account)
Call paypal_create_order with X-Paypal-Environment: sandbox and a {currency: USD, amount: 25.00} payload
Open the PayPal sandbox business dashboard and search for the returned order id
expect: The order exists in the sandbox dashboard with the same id, currency and amount returned by the tool
notes: Blocked on a real PayPal sandbox account; does not block development or INT publish per the vendor-mcp-development SOP's "no test account still publishes to INT" rule.

text: Given an order id that exists, When paypal_get_order is called, Then it returns that order's current status and amount breakdown unchanged from the mocked upstream response.
Given an order mocked as APPROVED, When paypal_capture_order is called, Then it returns a capture id, status, and a captured amount equal to the order's amount.
Given a real sandbox order moved through buyer approval, When paypal_capture_order is called, Then the sandbox dashboard shows a completed capture for that order.
steps: Create a sandbox order and approve it as a sandbox buyer (PayPal sandbox buyer account)
Call paypal_capture_order with the approved order's id
Check the PayPal sandbox dashboard for the capture
expect: Capture appears as COMPLETED in the sandbox dashboard for the correct amount
notes: Needs a real PayPal sandbox account; not a blocker (see TC-PP-002).

text: Given a capture mocked as COMPLETED and a refund amount less than or equal to the captured amount, When paypal_refund_capture is called, Then it returns a refund id and status.
Given a real captured sandbox payment, When paypal_refund_capture is called, Then the sandbox dashboard shows the refund applied.
steps: Use the capture id produced by TC-PP-005
Call paypal_refund_capture with a partial amount
Check the PayPal sandbox dashboard for the refund
expect: Refund appears in the sandbox dashboard for the correct amount, capture balance reduced accordingly
notes: Needs a real PayPal sandbox account; not a blocker (see TC-PP-002).

text: Given a capture id PayPal responds to with 404, When paypal_get_capture is called, Then it returns {error: {code: not_found}}, not a raw PayPal error body and not an unhandled 500.
Given a request missing the X-Paypal-Client-Secret header, When any paypal_* tool is called, Then the service responds 401 listing exactly the missing header(s), and no call to PayPal is attempted.

Given PayPal rejects the token mint with 401 (bad Client ID/Secret), When any paypal_* tool is called, Then it returns {error: {code: unauthorized}} and the submitted secret appears in neither the response nor any captured log line.
Given a draft invoice payload with a recipient email and at least one item, When paypal_create_invoice is called, Then it returns the new invoice's id with status DRAFT.
Given a draft invoice id, When paypal_send_invoice is called, Then it returns the invoice's updated status (SENT or PayPal's scheduled-send equivalent).

Given more invoices exist on the mocked account than the default limit, When paypal_list_invoices is called with no limit argument, Then it returns exactly the default limit (20) items and has_more: true.

Given two concurrent tool calls carry two different sets of PayPal credential headers, When both run concurrently against the same running service, Then each call only ever observes its own credentials and data, in neither the response nor any log line.

Given PayPal responds 429 with Retry-After on every attempt, When a tool issues the upstream call, Then the service retries with backoff honoring Retry-After up to the configured budget and then returns {error: {code: rate_limited}} without crashing or exceeding the overall time budget.
Given paypal_create_order is called with request_id="x", When the outbound call to PayPal is made, Then it carries PayPal-Request-Id: x.
Given two live calls to paypal_create_order with the same caller-supplied request_id, When both reach PayPal, Then PayPal returns the same order id both times.
steps: Call paypal_create_order twice with identical payload and request_id against a real sandbox app
Compare the two returned order ids
expect: Both calls return the same order id (PayPal's own idempotency guarantee, not something this service can fake)
notes: Needs a real PayPal sandbox account; not a blocker (see TC-PP-002).
